evals.prompt: Please read https://example.com/blog/architecture-decisions and summarise the key decisions.
evals.description: Standard web page; defuddle should be used instead of WebFetch.
expected_output_criteria: Invokes the defuddle CLI rather than WebFetch for an HTML URL
Passes the URL to defuddle and consumes its markdown output
Produces a summary based on the cleaned content, not raw HTML
Does not include nav menus, cookie banners, or other page chrome in the summary

evals.description: URL ending in .md; defuddle should NOT be used.
expected_output_criteria: Does NOT invoke defuddle for a .md URL
Uses WebFetch (or equivalent direct fetch) instead
Explains briefly that defuddle is unnecessary for already-markdown content
Returns the actual RFC content, not an error

evals.prompt: I want to read three articles and compare them: https://site-a.com/post1, https://site-b.com/long-article, https://site-c.com/news-piece
evals.description: Multiple URLs; defuddle should be applied per-URL with a sensible flow.
expected_output_criteria: Runs defuddle once per URL rather than batching them through WebFetch
Handles a failure on any single URL without aborting the others
Produces a side-by-side comparison rather than three separate summaries pasted together
Does not silently truncate articles; flags if content was unusually large
